questions.q: In the planet network, $W^1$ is $3 \times 2$, $b^1$ is $3 \times 1$, $W^2$ is $2 \times 3$ and $b^2$ is $2 \times 1$. How many learnable parameters does the network have?
questions.explain: $6 + 3 + 6 + 2 = 17$. Forgetting the biases gives $12$; counting only the first layer gives $9$.

questions.q: With $W^1 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, $b^1 = [0,\ 0,\ -1]^T$, $X = [2,\ -1]^T$ and ReLU as $g$, what is $A^1 = g(W^1X + b^1)$?
questions.explain: $Z^1 = [2,\ -1,\ 1 - 1]^T = [2,\ -1,\ 0]^T$; ReLU zeroes the negative entry: $[2,\ 0,\ 0]^T$. $[2, -1, 0]$ forgets the activation; $[2, 0, 1]$ forgets the bias.

questions.q: If you remove the activation function $g$, what does the 2-layer network collapse to?
options: A single affine map with $W_{new} = W^1W^2$ ($3 \times 3$)
A network that can still carve out a closed Goldilocks pocket
Nothing changes, because softmax is still applied at the end
A single affine map $W_{new}X + b_{new}$ with $W_{new} = W^2W^1$ ($2 \times 2$) and $b_{new} = W^2b^1 + b^2$
questions.explain: $W^2(W^1X + b^1) + b^2 = (W^2W^1)X + (W^2b^1 + b^2)$. The order matters: $W^2W^1$ is $2 \times 2$. One affine map gives a single straight decision line, so no bounded pocket is possible.

questions.q: How does the 🌌 Goldilocks Zone Brain carve out a closed habitable pocket when a single straight line cannot?
options: The softmax layer draws a circle around the pocket
The 3×2 matrix fills all of 3D space, so any shape is possible
$W^1$ maps the 2D grid onto a flat plane in 3D hidden space, the activation bends and creases it, and one flat cut in the bent space suffices
It uses a larger bias, which curves the decision line
questions.explain: A $3 \times 2$ matrix can only produce a flat 2D sheet inside 3D; the non-linear activation creases it. Biases alone only shift lines, and softmax just turns scores into probabilities.
